names.es: Pasteurización de huevo en cáscara (queda crudo)

source: instantaneousC (71°C) is the same USDA FoodSafety.gov figure as egg_cooking.json, included because CriticalControlPointSchema requires one, but it is NOT usable for this process — reaching it would cook the egg, defeating the entire point. heldC/heldSeconds (57°C / ~65 minutes) is a commonly-cited figure in food-science / extension literature for in-shell pasteurization that keeps the egg raw-textured (the process popularized academically at Kansas State University and used commercially by e.g. Davidson's Safest Choice eggs) — flagged explicitly: this repo has NOT independently verified the exact published minutes against a primary source, and exact commercial process parameters vary/are sometimes proprietary. Verify against a primary food-safety-authority source before relying on this for an actual production process.

metadata.note: advisoryOnly: false, unlike egg_cooking.json's runny-yolk case. A cooked-but-runny egg is an FDA-recognized 'increased risk, disclosed' practice a diner can knowingly accept. Serving raw egg to someone (a child, by name, per the request that motivated this file) with NO pasteurization step at all is not that — there is no equivalent 'disclosed and accepted' framing for silently skipping the one mitigation this process exists to provide, so a shortfall here is a hard reject regardless of SafetyPolicy.mode, not something even a human operator's warning-and-continue path should wave through by default.
metadata.whyNotJustUseEggCooking: egg_cooking.json's 63°C/15s or 71°C-instant points would cook/set the yolk — incompatible with a process whose whole purpose is keeping the egg raw. This is a genuinely different point on the FDA Food Code's real time-temperature curve, not a stricter or looser version of the same one; see thermal.ts's doc comment on why that schema only captures two anchor points, not the full curve — this CCP is a third, separate anchor for a different use case.
metadata.independentVerificationNote: Checked 2026-08-14 in direct response to an external scientific review's request to independently verify this figure. Found real, peer-reviewed corroboration, not a contradiction: Bermúdez-Aguirre & Niemira, "A review on egg pasteurization and disinfection: Traditional and novel processing technologies," Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety (2023), https://doi.org/10.1111/1541-4337.13088 — states "the standard pasteurization method for shell eggs is 57°C for 57.5 minutes," close to but shorter than this file's existing 65min. A second peer-reviewed CFD study (Applied Sciences, MDPI, 2025, large-egg 5-log-Salmonella-reduction figures bracketing 56°C/37.2min and 58°C/29.1min) is shorter still. Both corroborate that 65min carries real safety margin above what's needed, not that it's unsafely short — deliberately KEPT at 65min rather than tightened to the peer-reviewed figure: for a threshold gating whether raw egg is safe to serve someone with no other mitigation, the more conservative existing value was kept on purpose after this verification, not left unverified. See REFERENCES.md's 'Discussed, not yet embedded' section for the full citation trail.
